questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:

questions.q: If force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>F</mi><mo>)</mo></math>, velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>V</mi><mo>)</mo></math> and time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>)</mo></math> are considered as fundamental physical quantity, then dimensional formula of density will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The dimensional formula of force is

F=MLT-2

The dimensional formula of velocity is

V=LT-1

The formula for density is 

 Density =ML3=ML-3

Comparing the density dimensions with the assumed fundamental quantities in the question,
ML-3=FxVyTz⇒ML-3=MLT-2xLT-1y[T]z⇒ML-3=MxL(x+y)T-2x-y+z

Comparing the exponents,
x=1   ...(i)x+y=-3   ...(ii)-2x-y+z=0   ...(iii)

Solving equations (i), (ii) & (iii), we get

y=-4, z=-2.

The dimensions of density =FV-4T-2.

questions.q:
The equation of a circle is given by x2+y2=a2, where a is the radius. If the equation is modified to change the origin other than (0, 0), then find out the correct dimensions of A and B in a new equation :

x-At2+y-tB2=a2

The dimensions of t is given as T-1
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Principle of Homogeneity states that dimensions of each of the terms of a dimensional equation on both sides should be the same. Then,

x-At2+y-tB2=a2

For first term, 

At=x⇒A×1T=L

∴A=T1L1

For the second term,

tB=y

⇒1TB=L

⇒B=T-1L-1

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement (I) : Planck's constant and angular momentum have the same dimensions.

Statement (II) : Linear momentum and moment of force have the same dimensions.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The dimensions of the required quantities can be written as

E=hν⇒h=Eν⇒[h]=ML2T-2T-1=ML2T-1

[L]=mvr=MLT-1L=ML2 T-1

[p]=mv=MLT-1=ML1 T-1

[τ]=Fr=MLT-2L=ML2 T-2

where, h  is Planck's constant, L is angular momentum, p is linear momentum and τ is moment of force.

From the above analysis, it can be concluded that Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
